questions.text: Greenhill College provides a secure digital library. A Learner signs in to search academic resources, download licensed electronic items, reserve available print books, renew eligible loans and view borrowing history. A Librarian maintains resource records and processes returns. A Library Manager reviews overdue reports and manages accounts. Automated reminders alert learners about due dates. A print book cannot be downloaded. Explain two important differences between a Learner's authority and a Librarian's authority.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners can search, reserve/renew and access permitted resources; librarians can create/update resource records and process returns. Learners do not have the librarian's collection-maintenance rights.
aiRubric: Names at least two concrete differences
questions.aiReferenceNotes: An actor's system permissions should match their role and goals. Identify what each role is allowed to do. Give at least two clear differences. Explain that one role cannot simply do everything the other can. A manager has a third role; do not confuse library management with learner access.
questions.explanation:
An actor's system permissions should match their role and goals.

1. Identify what each role is allowed to do.
2. Give at least two clear differences.
3. Explain that one role cannot simply do everything the other can.

Example: Searching for a journal differs from publishing a new journal entry into the catalogue.

Student note: A manager has a third role; do not confuse library management with learner access.

study.title: Actor privileges
study.simple: An actor's system permissions should match their role and goals.
steps: Identify what each role is allowed to do.
Give at least two clear differences.
Explain that one role cannot simply do everything the other can.
study.example: Searching for a journal differs from publishing a new journal entry into the catalogue.
study.pitfall: A manager has a third role; do not confuse library management with learner access.
study.remember: Identify what each role is allowed to do.

questions.text: TrayGo serves local students who order meals from registered cafés. A Customer chooses a café, adds menu items to a cart, selects delivery and confirms payment. The Café may accept or reject an order. If accepted, it prepares the food and marks it ready. The platform assigns a Courier, who collects the meal, marks it in transit and delivers it. The Customer receives a status notice and may leave a rating. Payment failure stops the order before a café is notified. Draw a UML USE CASE diagram showing a system boundary, the external actor roles and the major goals they perform.
questions.correctAnswer: TrayGo system boundary containing Browse menu, Place order, Pay, Track order, Accept/reject order, Mark ready, Collect delivery, Update delivery, Rate experience. Customer linked to browse/place/pay/track/rate; Café linked to accept/reject/mark ready; Courier linked to collect/update delivery. Payment service optional external actor if modelled consistently.
aiRubric: Boundary with an appropriate system name
questions.aiReferenceNotes: An actor is a role outside the system. An oval describes a meaningful goal carried out through the system. List all external roles and their goals. Place goal ovals inside the system boundary. Connect relevant actors; do not model every internal calculation as an actor. Use case diagrams show who needs functions; they do not show detailed chronological steps.
questions.explanation:
An actor is a role outside the system. An oval describes a meaningful goal carried out through the system.

1. List all external roles and their goals.
2. Place goal ovals inside the system boundary.
3. Connect relevant actors; do not model every internal calculation as an actor.

Example: Customer connects to Place order; Café connects to Accept order; Courier connects to Update delivery.

Student note: Use case diagrams show who needs functions; they do not show detailed chronological steps.

questions.text: TrayGo serves local students who order meals from registered cafés. A Customer chooses a café, adds menu items to a cart, selects delivery and confirms payment. The Café may accept or reject an order. If accepted, it prepares the food and marks it ready. The platform assigns a Courier, who collects the meal, marks it in transit and delivers it. The Customer receives a status notice and may leave a rating. Payment failure stops the order before a café is notified. Draw an ACTIVITY diagram for a successful order, including payment failure and café rejection paths. Include start/end nodes, actions, arrows and decisions.
questions.correctAnswer: Start -> Customer selects café -> adds items -> checkout -> calculate total -> choose payment -> validate payment [failure: display failure then End/retry] [success: send order to café] -> café decision [reject: notify customer and cancel/end] [accept: prepare food -> mark ready] -> assign courier -> courier collects -> in transit -> delivered -> notify customer -> optional rate -> End. Guarded flows at decisions.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Activity diagrams show ordered actions, decision points and alternative outcomes in a process. Start with a filled initial circle. Place rounded action boxes and diamond decisions in time order. Label branches such as [approved] and [declined], then end each completed path. Use case diagrams show user goals; activity diagrams show the workflow that achieves a goal.
questions.explanation:
Activity diagrams show ordered actions, decision points and alternative outcomes in a process.

1. Start with a filled initial circle.
2. Place rounded action boxes and diamond decisions in time order.
3. Label branches such as [approved] and [declined], then end each completed path.

Example: A failed payment must not continue directly into preparation.

Student note: Use case diagrams show user goals; activity diagrams show the workflow that achieves a goal.
